results.title: Gemini 1.5: Unlocking multimodal understanding across millions of tokens of context (arXiv:2403.05530)
results.snippet: The official technical report detailing Gemini 1.5's long context capabilities. Key technical details: - Achieves up to 10 million tokens context (1M in production API) - Uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture to enable the long context - Submitted March 8, 2024, revised Dec 16, 2024 - Authors: Petko Georgiev, Ving Ian Lei, Ryan Burnell, et al.

results.title: Wikipedia - Gemini context window specs
results.snippet: Context lengths by variant: - 1.0 Nano-1: 32,768 tokens - 1.0 Nano-2: 32,768 tokens - 1.0 Pro: Not publicly known - 1.0 Ultra: Not publicly known - 1.5 Pro: 10,000,000 tokens (10M) internally, 1M tokens in production API - 1.5 Mini: Not publicly known. As Gemini is multimodal, each context window can contain multiple forms of input interleaved in any order (text, picture, video, audio). Audio sampled at 16kHz converted to tokens by Universal Speech Model. Video inputted as sequence of images.

results.title: Google DeepMind - Current models
results.snippet: Current lineup: Gemini 3.5 Flash, 3.1 Pro, 3.1 Deep Think, 3.1 Flash-Lite. Benchmark table shows long context performance: MRCR v2 (8-needle) test - 3.5 Flash: 77.3% at 128k (average), 26.6% at 1M (pointwise); 3 Flash: 67.2% at 128k, 22.1% at 1M; 3.1 Pro: 84.9% at 128k, 26.3% at 1M. The models support native audio output (2.5 Pro and Flash+).

results.title: Gemini (language model) - Wikipedia - Updates section
results.snippet: February 2024: Google launched Gemini 1.5 describing it as a more powerful model than 1.0 Ultra. Changes include a new architecture, a mixture-of-experts approach, and a larger one-million-token context window.
